instructions: Cut the 6 bacon slices into 1-inch pieces. Dice the onion, mince 2 of the garlic cloves and slice the mushrooms thick. Cut 8 slices of baguette about 1 inch thick, and cut the last garlic clove in half.
Put a large deep skillet over medium-high heat and add the bacon. Cook for 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until crisp. Transfer the bacon to a plate.
Pour off all but about 2 tbsp of the bacon fat into a small bowl and keep it for the toast.
Add the onion and minced garlic to the skillet and cook for 2 minutes, until the onion is soft. Add the mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes, until they've released their liquid.
Sprinkle the flour over the top and stir for 1 minute, until it's golden.
Add the bay leaf, thyme, sugar, 1/2 tsp of the salt and the pepper. Pour in the wine and broth and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom. Return the bacon to the pan.
Bring it to a boil, then turn the heat to medium-low and simmer, uncovered, for 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce is thick enough to coat a spoon.

Meanwhile, heat a second skillet over medium-high heat with the reserved bacon fat. Toast the baguette slices for 2 minutes per side, until golden. Rub the cut side of the halved garlic clove over each toast.
Fill a wide pot with about 2 inches of water, add the 3 tbsp vinegar and bring it to a gentle simmer. Don't let it boil hard.

Crack 4 of the eggs, one at a time, into a small cup. Stir the water to make a slow whirlpool and slide each egg into the middle. Poach for 3 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks still jiggle. Lift them out with a slotted spoon onto a plate lined with paper towels. Poach the other 4 eggs the same way.
Take the bay leaf out of the sauce. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch of the remaining 1/4 tsp salt.
Put 2 toasts on each plate and spoon the sauce over them. Top each with 2 poached eggs and scatter on the chopped parsley.
method_notes: Curious Cuisiniere (the lead) fries bacon, cooks onion, garlic and mushrooms in the fat, stirs in flour, then builds a red wine and beef broth sauce with bay, thyme and a little sugar, with garlic toast and eggs poached in vinegar water. Custrd simmers its sauce 12 minutes and Taste France reduces the wine by two thirds with veal stock; Djalali Cooks simmers about 50 minutes. No version has 20 ratings. This follows the lead with less wine and broth and a 12 minute simmer so it fits half an hour, 2 eggs a person for a main, and no pearl onions.

sources.name: Djalali Cooks
